name: The Love Bomber
subtitle: Too much, too fast
early_signs: Says 'I love you' or 'you're my person' within days or weeks
Constant texting — feels like surveillance if you don't reply fast
Grand romantic gestures very early (gifts, planning future trips)
Claims you're different from everyone they've ever met
Pushes for exclusivity before you've barely met
how_it_feels: Intoxicating at first — like you're the main character of a movie. Then slowly unsettling, like the movie is moving too fast.
red_flags: Gets upset or withdrawn when you don't match their intensity
Uses the grand gestures to guilt you into reciprocating feelings
Isolates you from friends/family ('I want you all to myself')
The intensity disappears suddenly if you set any limit
how_to_respond: You can like someone AND slow things down. Try: 'I really enjoy spending time with you, and I need things to move a bit more gradually — can we do that?' If they respect it, great. If they get angry or sad-manipulate you, that tells you everything.
nuance_note: Not everyone who's intense is a Love Bomber. Some people are just very expressive and enthusiastic. The key difference is: do they respect your pace when you communicate it?

name: The Slow Burner
subtitle: Depth over drama
early_signs: Takes time before they open up emotionally
Consistent but not overwhelming — texts regularly, doesn't flood
Actions match words over time, not all at once
Might seem reserved early but becomes warmer with trust
how_it_feels: Comfortable and real, like something that grows naturally. Can feel uncertain early on because there's no dramatic flash.
green_flags: Shows up reliably over weeks and months
Respects your pace as well as their own
Doesn't play games — just naturally cautious with their heart
red_flags: Using 'slow burn' as an excuse to avoid any real emotional commitment indefinitely
Never moves forward even when trust is clearly established
how_to_respond: Give it time. Don't mistake quietness for disinterest. Slow Burners often become the most consistent and genuine partners. Check in with words if you feel unsure.
nuance_note: Slow Burners are often mistaken for people who aren't interested. The difference: do they keep showing up, even if quietly?

name: The Hot-and-Cold
subtitle: The emotional rollercoaster
early_signs: Very intense and present one week, distant and unresponsive the next
Their availability depends entirely on their mood
Plans get made and cancelled in cycles
Messages shift from warm to cold without explanation
how_it_feels: Like being in an emotional whirlpool. You're never sure where you stand, so you work extra hard to get the 'hot' version back.
red_flags: The coldness comes as punishment or after you set a boundary
You're changing your behaviour to avoid triggering the cold phase
They never acknowledge the pattern when you bring it up
how_to_respond: Name it calmly: 'I've noticed things feel really warm sometimes and then I don't hear from you for days — can we talk about that?' Their reaction is your data. Genuine care = willingness to discuss. Dismissal = information.
nuance_note: Sometimes Hot-and-Cold behaviour comes from anxiety or avoidant attachment — it's not always intentional. But regardless of cause, you deserve consistency.

name: The Almost-Something
subtitle: The one that never quite lands
early_signs: Everything feels relationship-ish but there's always a reason it's 'not the right time'
Acts like a partner privately but doesn't want a label publicly
Has genuine feelings but a deep fear of commitment
May use ambiguity to protect themselves from risk
how_it_feels: Like standing at a door that's almost open. Hopeful and frustrating in equal measure.
green_flags: Genuinely cares about you and shows it
Is honest about their fear of commitment (even if that's hard to hear)
Is willing to have the conversation, even if it's scary for them
red_flags: Uses ambiguity manipulatively to keep you available while they decide
Refuses any conversation about 'what are we' indefinitely
Expects relationship-level commitment from you without offering it back
how_to_respond: Have the DTR conversation. Something like: 'I've been enjoying our time together and I want to be honest — I'm looking for something real. Are you in a place for that?' Then listen to their answer carefully, not just their words.
nuance_note: Not every Almost-Something is stringing you along. Some people are genuinely scared. The question is: are they scared AND willing to work on it?

name: The Bestie-Zone Keeper
subtitle: Deeply valued — as a friend
early_signs: Introduces you to their inner circle as a friend very early
Genuinely loves spending time with you but in a friendly way
Doesn't mirror romantic signals even when you give them
Talks about other people they're interested in
how_it_feels: Confusing when you have feelings. Their warmth feels like something more — until it doesn't.
green_flags: Values you genuinely and treats you well
Is honest about where they stand if asked directly
Keeps the friendship solid even when things are complicated
red_flags: Keeps you emotionally close while pursuing others — using your support without acknowledging your feelings
Gives mixed signals that seem intentional
how_to_respond: If you have feelings, they deserve to be expressed once — clearly and without pressure. 'I've developed feelings for you and I wanted to be honest, even if it changes things.' Their response is information. A friendship built on hidden feelings isn't fair to either of you.
nuance_note: Rejection is valid and not a personal failing. The Bestie-Zone Keeper isn't doing anything wrong by not having romantic feelings — it's just life. Sometimes friendship becomes something real later; sometimes it doesn't.

name: The Showboater
subtitle: The highlight reel, all day
early_signs: Leads with credentials, wealth, or status in early conversations
Stories about themselves dominate the conversation
Name-drops often — places they've been, people they know, things they own
Gets noticeably less engaged when the topic isn't about them
how_it_feels: Impressive at first. Tiring very quickly.
green_flags: Can laugh at themselves when pointed out gently
Has substance beneath the performance — the showboating comes from nerves, not narcissism
red_flags: Never asks questions about you
Gets defensive or cold when the spotlight shifts
Uses status or gifts to create a power imbalance
how_to_respond: See if they can hold a conversation that's equally about you. Ask questions and notice if they engage or redirect. You can also gently name it: 'I'd love to hear about you — the real stuff, not just the highlights.'
nuance_note: Some Showboating is just nerves or cultural habit. The important question: do they actually care to know YOU?

name: The Ghost
subtitle: Now you see them, now you don't
early_signs: Goes quiet without explanation for days
Always has vague reasons for disappearing
Patterns of reappearing as if nothing happened
Never initiates contact consistently
how_it_feels: Like being suspended in uncertainty. You check your phone too much. You second-guess everything you said.
red_flags: Disappears specifically after moments of depth or vulnerability
Re-appears whenever they want something — attention, support, company
Knows you're bothered by the silence and continues anyway
how_to_respond: One follow-up is okay. Two is too many. After one unanswered check-in, stop reaching out. Your peace matters more than their comfort. If they come back, decide based on whether they acknowledge the disappearance.
nuance_note: Some people ghost because of their own anxiety and avoidance — not because of you. That doesn't make it okay, but it helps to not take it personally.

name: The Secure One
subtitle: Rare. Real. Worth it.
early_signs: Communicates clearly without playing games
Respects your boundaries without making it weird
Is honest about what they want — even when it's scary
Doesn't need to be constantly reassured, and doesn't withhold reassurance from you
how_it_feels: Calm. Surprisingly unfamiliar if you're used to drama. Like breathing out.
green_flags: Brings up difficult topics with care, not as weaponised 'honesty'
Has their own full life and doesn't need you to complete them
Apologises when they're wrong — genuinely, not strategically
how_to_respond: Meet their energy. Don't self-sabotage by creating drama because calm feels unfamiliar. Secure people are attracted to people who are doing the work on themselves.
nuance_note: Nobody is perfectly Secure all the time — we all have harder moments. The Secure One's difference is: they're willing to reflect, communicate, and grow.
